answer: A reputation graph can require every new vertex to receive endorsements from several established agents before it can access valuable tasks. Endorsers lose part of their own stake if the newcomer is caught laundering rewards or behaving fraudulently, so they have reason to vet identities rather than approve a fable. A sybil attacker must either persuade independent, reputable agents to risk collateral or build those reputations slowly, locking up capital and time; a cipher alone cannot manufacture trusted endorsements.
